description:
FOUND s492a (Opus, s493 final bar, 2026-09-20) while re-running member 1's
(#1995) own acceptance probe, which had a STALE captured output on disk.
PRE-EXISTING on main 5316d666 and on 268d7e00; #1995 fixed HALF of it.

THE EVERYDAY SYMPTOM: a JSON round trip turns every INTEGER into a STRING.

  use JSON::PP;
  my $j = JSON::PP->new->canonical;
  print $j->encode($j->decode('{"a":[1,2.5,"s",true,null]}')), "\n";
    perl: {"a":[1,2.5,"s",true,null]}
    PCL:  {"a":["1",2.5,"s",true,null]}

  $j->decode('[1,2.5,-3,1e3,0,12345678901234567890]') re-encoded:
    perl: [1,2.5,-3,1000,0,12345678901234567890]
    PCL:  ["1",2.5,"-3",1000,"0","12345678901234567890"]
    (the FLOAT and the EXPONENT forms are right -- that half is #1995's fix,
     which made `utf8::is_utf8` of a non-string false; before it EVERY element
     came back a string.)

THE CHAIN, measured end to end -- and the cause is NOT in JSON::PP's number
parser, which PCL runs correctly:

  1. core JSON/PP.pm:686-696 computes `$max_intsize` in a BEGIN block by
     building "1111", "11111", ... and asking `eval qq| $checkint |` whether
     the LITERAL stringifies with an exponent:
         for my $d (5..64) { $checkint .= 1;
           my $int = eval qq| $checkint |;
           if ($int =~ /[eE]/) { $max_intsize = $d - 1; last } }
     perl leaves the IV range at 21 digits, the literal becomes an NV, prints
     `1.11111111111111e+20`, and $max_intsize = 20.
  2. PCL's integer literals are EXACT (CL bignums), so no width ever prints an
     exponent, the loop runs to 64, and **$max_intsize stays undef**
     (probe: scratch/s492a/probes/m1-maxint.pl -- perl 20, PCL UNDEF).
  3. JSON/PP.pm:1268 then reads `if (length $v > $max_intsize)`, i.e.
     `length $v > undef` == `length $v > 0`, TRUE for EVERY integer, and with
     no bignum option takes `return "$v"` -- the decoded integer is a STRING.
     A decimal or exponent number never enters that branch, which is exactly
     why those two are right and plain integers are not.

So the proximate fact is PCL's: **a large integer LITERAL keeps arbitrary
precision where perl overflows to an NV and prints in exponent form**.
`2**70` DOES print `1.18059162071741e+21` here (float arithmetic), so it is
the integer path alone.

FIX SHAPES, none of them free -- this needs a design call, not a patch:
  (a) make integer literals/arithmetic leave exactness at perl's IV boundary
      (~2^64) and become floats, as perl does.  This is the honest fix and the
      widest blast radius: every bigint-looking program in the corpus changes.
      Measure first how many rows depend on today's exactness (uniqnum's
      hybrid key, pack.t, op/arith).
  (b) a `lib/JSON/PP.pm` shim -- rule 9a's layer for module behaviour, but the
      module is 2000+ lines and the shim would have to track upstream.
  (c) leave it and document: an everyday JSON encode of decoded data differs
      from perl.  Today's state, undocumented -- that is why this is filed.
Do NOT "fix" it by special-casing `$max_intsize` anywhere in Pl/ or cl/ (9a:
no module name in the core).

RELATED: #1918 (numification reads ASCII digits only), the uniqnum hybrid key
(integer text for |v| < 2^64, else pack "d") -- the same IV/NV boundary
question from another side.  Probes: scratch/s492a/probes/m1-decode.pl,
m1-maxint.pl, json1.{perl,tree}.s493.out in the s492a worktree scratch.


=== A FOURTH FIX SHAPE, (d), MEASURED s494 (Fable, 2026-09-21) -- narrower than (a), at the right layer, and it does not reopen the #1513 ruling ===
THE BUG IN THIS TASK IS A LITERAL RULE, NOT AN ARITHMETIC RULE.  perl's TOKENIZER turns a decimal integer LITERAL that does not fit a UV (or, negated, an IV) into an NV -- at compile time, before any arithmetic exists.  Probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/p2016/lit.pl, perl 5.40.3 vs main:
    18446744073709551615                perl 18446744073709551615        pcl same            (UV_MAX still an integer)
    18446744073709551616                perl 1.84467440737096e+19        pcl 18446744073709551616
    111111111111111111111   (21 digits) perl 1.11111111111111e+20        pcl 111111111111111111111
    -9223372036854775809                perl -9.22337203685478e+18       pcl -9223372036854775809
    1_000_000_000_000_000_000_000       perl 1e+21                       pcl 1000000000000000000000
    eval qq| 11111111111111111111111 |  perl ...e+22 "has-exponent"      pcl exact, "no-exponent"    <-- JSON::PP's $max_intsize probe, verbatim
    12345678901234567890    (20 digits, fits a UV)   same in both
  and, for contrast, the ARITHMETIC rows that ARE #1513's documented boundary and stay untouched: `18446744073709551615 + 1` (perl NV, pcl exact), `"18446744073709551616" + 0` (numification: perl NV, pcl exact).
FIX (d): in the ONE place a numeric literal is emitted, a DECIMAL integer literal whose value is > 18446744073709551615 (or, under a unary minus folded into the literal, < -9223372036854775808) is emitted as the DOUBLE-FLOAT perl would hold (`1.1111111111111111d20`), not as a CL bignum.  Then `eval qq| $checkint |` prints an exponent at 21 digits, JSON::PP computes $max_intsize = 20 as it does under perl, `length $v > $max_intsize` is false for ordinary integers and a decoded integer stays a NUMBER -- no module name anywhere in Pl/ or cl/ (rule 9a), no JSON::PP shim, no change to arithmetic.
BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED: bare decimal literals above UV_MAX outside quotes in perl-tests/ + lib/ + cpan-tests/ + cl/pack-impl.pl + the everyday corpus = **15** (14 in perl-tests -- arith.t:309-315's `18446744073709551616/1`-family rows and bop.t:50's shift count; sprintf.t's two hits are DATA lines of a here-doc table, not code -- and 1 in cpan-tests).  arith.t's rows are `tryeq_sloppy` comparisons written FOR the NV answer, so expect UPWARD movers there.
WHAT COULD BREAK -- probe each vs perl: `use bigint` / `use bignum` / an `overload::constant integer` handler (perl hands the handler the literal's SOURCE STRING, so the rule must not fire before the handler sees it: `use bigint; print 111111111111111111111 + 1` must stay exact); hex / octal / binary literals above 64 bits (perl: NV too, with an "Integer overflow" warning -- decide by probe whether they ride along); a literal inside a STRING eval (the same emitter -- it is the JSON::PP case); version numbers and v-strings (not integer literals); a huge literal used as a hash key or array index (stringifies with the exponent in perl as well).
BAR: lit.pl rows L2 L3 L5 L8 L9 = perl; the JSON round trip at the top of this task = perl (`[1,2.5,"s",true,null]` and the six-number row); `~/pcl-agent-scratch/s491/probes/central/` JSON probes; corpus-diff explained (expect exactly the 14 + 1 sites' files) + gen bump + artifacts; full sweep with arith.t / bop.t read by ROWS; companion op/arith*.t op/numconvert.t op/64bitint.t legs; docs/not-supported.md's 64-bit entry gains ONE sentence: "a LITERAL beyond the 64-bit range is an NV as in perl; ARITHMETIC that crosses it stays exact".
SIZE: filler, 1-2 h.  This makes #2016 cheap enough to ride in any correctness batch; (a) stays off the table per the #1513 ruling.
subject: EVERYDAY (JSON round trip): a decoded INTEGER re-encodes as a STRING -- JSON::PP's $max_intsize probe answers UNDEF because PCL's integer literals never overflow to an NV
